mcqs.question: Consider the following two systems: (i) a simple pendulum released from a small angle, and (ii) a mass attached to a vertical spring that is hanging motionless. Which statement correctly identifies the equilibrium position for an oscillating system?

options.A: The position of the mass when the spring is neither stretched nor compressed (its natural length).
options.B: The extreme point where the pendulum reaches its maximum angular displacement.
options.C: The point where the mass attached to the spring is moving upward with maximum speed.
options.D: The position where the spring is stretched by an external constant force and held fixed.

mcqs.answer: The position of the mass when the spring is neither stretched nor compressed (its natural length).
mcqs.explanation: The equilibrium position of an oscillating system is the point where the net restoring force is zero. For a vertical spring, this occurs when the spring is at its natural length, i.e., neither stretched nor compressed. At this point the mass can pass through without any net force acting on it. The other options describe extreme or non‑equilibrium conditions.

mcqs.question: In simple harmonic motion, the amplitude is:

options.A: The maximum displacement of the oscillating body from its equilibrium position.
options.B: The time taken for one complete oscillation.
options.C: The number of oscillations per second.
options.D: The average speed of the body during oscillation.

mcqs.answer: The maximum displacement of the oscillating body from its equilibrium position.
mcqs.explanation: Amplitude is defined as the greatest distance the system moves away from its equilibrium position during an oscillation. It is a measure of the size of the oscillation, not of time, frequency, or speed. Options B, C and D refer to period, frequency, and speed respectively, which are different quantities.

mcqs.question: The time period of an oscillating system is:

options.A: The time taken for one complete oscillation.
options.B: The number of oscillations that occur in one second.
options.D: The magnitude of the restoring force.

mcqs.answer: The time taken for one complete oscillation.
mcqs.explanation: The period (T) is the duration of a single full cycle of motion. It is measured in seconds. Frequency (option B) is the reciprocal of the period. Amplitude (option C) and restoring force (option D) are unrelated to the definition of period.

mcqs.question: Frequency of a periodic motion is defined as:

options.A: The number of complete oscillations per unit time.
options.B: The time taken for one complete oscillation.
options.C: The maximum displacement from the equilibrium position.
options.D: The restoring force acting on the system.

mcqs.answer: The number of complete oscillations per unit time.
mcqs.explanation: Frequency (f) measures how many cycles occur each second and is expressed in hertz (Hz). It is the reciprocal of the period (T). Options B, C, and D describe period, amplitude, and force respectively, not frequency.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines periodic motion and distinguishes it from non‑periodic motion?

options.A: Motion that repeats at regular time intervals, unlike motion that does not repeat.
options.B: Motion that occurs only once, unlike continuous motion.
options.C: Motion with constant speed, unlike motion with variable speed.
options.D: Motion confined to a straight line, unlike circular motion.

mcqs.answer: Motion that repeats at regular time intervals, unlike motion that does not repeat.
mcqs.explanation: Periodic motion is characterized by a pattern that recurs after a fixed time interval (the period). Non‑periodic motion lacks such regular repetition. Options B, C, and D describe unrelated characteristics.

mcqs.question: A child on a swing moves back and forth repeatedly about a central position. Which description best defines the type of motion shown?
mcqs.explanation: Oscillatory motion is any motion that repeats about an equilibrium (central) position, such as the back‑and‑forth movement of a swing. Uniform linear motion (B) is straight‑line with constant speed, rotational motion (C) involves rotation about an axis, and random motion (D) lacks a regular pattern.

mcqs.question: A block attached to a horizontal spring is pulled 5 cm to the right and released. While it oscillates, at which point is the equilibrium position?

options.A: When the block passes through the undisturbed position of the spring (neither stretched nor compressed).
options.B: At the farthest right point of the motion.
options.C: At the farthest left point of the motion.
options.D: When the block is momentarily at rest at the extreme displacement.

mcqs.answer: When the block passes through the undisturbed position of the spring (neither stretched nor compressed).
mcqs.explanation: The equilibrium position is where the net restoring force on the block is zero, i.e., the spring is at its natural length. The block passes this point twice each cycle with maximum speed. Options B and C are extreme positions, and D describes a momentary rest at an extreme, not equilibrium.

mcqs.question: A simple pendulum is pulled to a maximum angular displacement of 15° and released. What term describes this maximum angular displacement?
mcqs.explanation: Amplitude is the greatest extent of displacement from the equilibrium position. For a pendulum, this is the maximum angular displacement. Frequency (B) is oscillations per second, period (C) is time for one oscillation, and phase (D) indicates the position within a cycle.
